factors.name: General size and connectivity complexity
factors.summary: With a single unrotated factor, nearly all measures load on it. Size, Control flow complexity and Number of duplicate tasks load at about 0.99, and the connector degree and connectivity measures load at 0.86–0.96, so larger nets also have more and busier connectors and more arcs per node. Density loads negatively (-0.73), as expected because density falls as nets grow, while Separability loads only moderately (0.44, communality 0.19) and is poorly represented.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.73 exceeds the 0.6 threshold, so the 288 nets are suitable for factor analysis. The first eigenvalue (6.25) dominates and the second is below 1, so a single factor was retained; it explains 76% of the variance. It is a general complexity factor: model size, control-flow branching, duplicate or silent transitions and connector degrees vary together, and density varies in the opposite direction. Sequentiality and Connector Mismatch were removed for low MSA, and Connector Heterogeneity, Token split and Number of empty sequence flows were removed because they were constant. The data therefore give no information on concurrency-specific dimensions.
caveats: Several loadings near 1 and eigenvalues close to zero suggest near-redundant measures (e.g. Size, Control flow complexity and Number of duplicate tasks), possibly driven by how the discovery algorithms build the nets.
Separability is weakly explained by the factor (communality 0.19) and may reflect a distinct aspect not captured here.
Constant measures (Connector Heterogeneity, Token split, Number of empty sequence flows) suggest the nets contain no parallel connectors, which limits generalization to concurrent models.
The one-factor result depends on this dataset and on the measures retained after the MSA filter; it describes shared variance, not causal structure.
